questions.question: What is the minimum age to become Rajya Sabha member?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30 years**__.

__
 
• The minimum age of thirty years is fixed for membership in the Upper House.
 
• It is the upper house, with smaller membership than the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
 
• It is the federal chamber, i.e., a House elected by the elected members of Assemblies of the States and two Union Territories in which States were not given equal representation.
 
• ​Qualifications
 
• Article 84 of the Constitution lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament.
 
• A person to be qualified for membership of the Rajya Sabha should possess the following qualifications:
 
• He must be a citizen of India and make and subscribe before some person authorized on that behalf by the Election Commission an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the Third Schedule to the Constitution.
 
• He must be not less than 30 years of age;
 
• He must possess such other qualifications as may be prescribed on that behalf by or under any law made by Parliament.

questions.question: By maternal descent, Mughals were descendants of?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Genghis Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Mughals:

 
 
• The Mughals were descendants of two great lineages of rulers.
 
• From their mother’s side, they were descendants of Genghis Khan (died 1227), the Mongol ruler who ruled over parts of China and Central Asia.
 
• From their father’s side, they were the successors of Timur (who died in 1404), the ruler of Iran, Iraq and modern-day Turkey.
 
• However, the Mughals did not like to be called Mughal or Mongol.
 
• This was because Genghis Khan’s memory was associated with the massacre of innumerable people.
 
• It was also linked with the Uzbeks, their Mongol competitors.
 
• On the other hand, the Mughals were proud of their Timurid ancestry, not least of all because their great ancestor had captured Delhi in 1398.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Timur**

 
 
• In 1398 A.D., the Timur or Tamerlane invaded India during the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud, the last king of the Tughlaq dynasty.
 
• Attacking the Delhi Sultanate ruled by Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq.
 
• He started his journey from Samarkand. After crossing the Sindh river, he entered Punjab.
 
• He crossed Indus and captured Multan, and just walked over to Delhi without much resistance.
 
• Tamerlane was a Turco-Mongol, who founded the Timurid Empire.
 
 

 
• Alexander__

 __
 
• Alexander__, the invaded India in the year __326 BC__.
 
• In 326 BC, Alexander invaded India, after crossing the river Indus he advanced towards Taxila.
 
• The Battle of the Hydaspes was fought in 326 BC between Alexander the Great and King Porus of the Paurava kingdom on the banks of the Jhelum River (known to the Greeks as Hydaspes) in the Punjab region.
 
• Alexander captured Porus and, like the other local rulers he had defeated, allowed him to continue to govern his territory.
 
• Alexander the Great was a king (basileus) of the ancient Greek kingdom of Macedon.

questions.question: Who set up the Asiatic Society of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __William Jones​.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Asiatic Society of Bengal, a scholarly society founded on January 15, 1784, by Sir William Jones.
 
• The Asiatic Society had the support and encouragement of Warren- Hastings, The Governor-General of Bengal, though he declined its presidency.
 
• Indian first admitted as a member in 1829, and its Headquarters are in Kolkata.
 
• The society owns an art collection that includes paintings by peter paul Rubens and Joshua Reynolds.
 
• The Sanskrit section of Society contains more than 27,000 books, manuscripts, prints, coins, and engravings.
 
• The journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal published regularly. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Robert Clive**

 
• Robert Clive the first English Governor of Bengal presidency made a settlement with the Nawab of Awadh in 1765, this settlement was also referred to as the First Treaty of Allahabad.
 
• Robert Clive, who was one of the founders of the establishment of British supremacy in India, came to India in the year 1743.
 
• Robert Clive was the First Governor of Bengal at the time of the company's rule who took office in 1758 after the assassination of the Nawab in Murshidabad in 1757.
 
• Dual Administration was introduced in the year 1765 by Robert Clive.
 
• Dual Administration divided the administration of Bengal into two parts.
 
 
• Diwani: It meant to Right to collect revenue (lay in the hands of the British).
 
• Nizamat: means Administration, which will be administered by Nawab of Bengal.
 
 

** Warren Hastings **

 
• The first governor-general in India (of Bengal) was Warren Hastings in 1773.
 
• He started his career as a writer (clerk) in the East India Company at Calcutta in 1750.
 
• Established revenue board in 1772.
 
• He Abolished the dual system of governance.
 
• Warren Hastings laid the foundation of civil service and Lord Cornwallis reformed, modernized, and rationalized it.

questions.question: The word agriculture is derived from the Latin words ager and culture. What does ‘ager’ mean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agriculture**

 
 
• Agriculture can be defined as the **art **and **science** of cultivating crops and rearing livestock for man use.
 
• It is a science because it involves the use of scientific methods for the production of both plants and animals it equally involves the application of scientific and technological knowledge.
 
 
 
• Soil
 
 
• Plants obtain inorganic elements from the soil, which serves as a natural medium for land plants. 
 
• Soil is the outer loose layer that covers the surface of Earth.
 
• Soil quality is a major determinant, along with climate, of plant distribution and growth.
 
• Soil quality depends not only on the chemical composition of the soil but also on the topography (regional surface features) and the presence of living organisms.
 
• In agriculture, the history of the soil, such as the cultivating practices and previous crops, modify the characteristics and fertility of that soil.
 
• Soil develops very slowly over long periods of time, and its formation results from natural and environmental forces acting on minerals, rock, and organic compounds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rocks**

 
 
• The earth's crust is made up of various types of rocks, differing from one another in texture, structure, colour, permeability, mode of occurrence, and degree of resistance to denudation.

questions.question: Which state has the highest reserves of graphite in India, as of April 2022?
questions.solution:

• **Graphite **is a kind of** crystalline carbon that occurs naturally.**
 
• The mineral graphite can be found in metamorphic and igneous rocks.
 
• **It is very soft, cleaves easily, and has a very low specific gravity.**
 
• It is the **only nonmetal that is a good electrical conductor.**
 
• Because of its greasy texture, it is also known as a dry lubricant.

Collective responsibility of the executive to the legislature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Undissolvable lower house**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the Parliamentary system, the head of the state may be a monarch or a President, but both of these positions are ceremonial.
 
• The head of the government, who is generally called the Prime Minister, is the real head.
 
• Thus all the real executive powers are vested in the Prime Minister.
 
• Articles 74 and 75 deal with the parliamentary system at the centre and Articles 163 and Article 164 deal with the Parliamentary system at the states.
 
• **Elements and features of a Parliamentary system are:-**
 
 
• Nominal and Real head.
 
• The executive is a part of the Legislature
 
• Majority party rule
 
• Collective responsibility
 
• The prime minister is the centre of power
 
• A Parliamentary opposition
 
• Independent Civil Service
 
• Bicameral Legislature
 
• Secrecy
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In the parliamentary form of government, there will be no separation of powers.**
 
• Here the executive will be part of the legislature.
 
• In the case of the presidential form of **government, legislative and executive are separate from each other.**
 
• The most defining feature of the parliamentary form of government: **the executive is answerable to the legislature, unlike the presidential form of government, where the executive is not answerable to the legislature. **
 
• **The parliamentary form of government defines the governing mechanism of the state and the division of power is not decided by the form of government.**

questions.question: In India, the second census of the 21st century was conducted in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2011**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In India, the second census** of the **21st century** was conducted in **2011**.
 
• As per the Census of India 2011, the population density of India was 382 per square km.
 
• The Indian Census is the most credible source of information on Demography (Population characteristics), Economic Activity, Literacy and Education, Housing Household Amenities, Urbanisation, Fertility and Mortality, etc. 
 
• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of the Country.
 
• Census was introduced in India during the era of Lord Mayo in the year 1872. It came into force in 1881.
 
• This census was conducted under the guidance of Mr. C. Chandramouli.
 
• The slogan of census 2011 was ‘Our Census, Our future’.
 
• The population of the nation as per the provisional figures of Census 2011 was 1210.19 million of which 623.7 million (51.54%) were males and 586.46 million (48.46%) were females. Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India its population is more than the population of Brazil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The next census was about to be conducted in 2021.
 
• The census was about to be conducted in two phases.
 
• 
 The planned rounds for the Census 2021 are given below:

 
 
• ​The first phase – House listing operations will be conducted in any two months chosen by the respective states between** April and September 2020.**
 
• The second phase – Actual population enumeration will be done from **February 9 to February 28, 2021.**
 
• Final phase – Revision round of the above two phases from** March 1 to March 5, 2021.**

questions.question: Who among the following legendary Kathak dancers passed away in January 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Birju Maharaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kathak legend Pandit Birju Maharaj passed away (age 83) in January 2022.
 
• Birju Maharaj was a descendant of the Maharaj family of Kathak dancers which includes his two uncles, Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj, and his father and guru, Acchan Maharaj.
 
• He was the recipient of numerous awards for his contributions to the performing arts, including the Padma Vibhushan in 1986.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• In 2021, a book on his life, titled Nritya Samrat Pt. Birju Maharaj was launched.
 
• The book is a compilation of 96 (22 in English and 70 in Hindi) short essays written by his disciples, associates, admirers and senior artists, associates, and well-wishers from around the world.
 
• It has been put together by Nandkishore Kapote, a senior disciple of Birju Maharaj.
 
• Awards received by him include:
 
 
• Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1964.
 
• Nritya Choodamani Award by Sri Krishna Gana Sabha in 1986.
 
• Kalidas Samman in 1987.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar Puraskar in 2002.

questions.question: Since which year has the AFSPA been started?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1958**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act (AFSPA)

 
 
• It is a Parliamentary act that grants special powers to the Indian Armed Forces and the state and paramilitary forces in areas classified as “disturbed areas”.
 
• The objective to implement the AFSPA Act is to maintain law and order in the disturbed areas. 
 
• It gives powers to the army, state, and central police forces to shoot to kill, search houses and destroy any property that is “likely” to be used by insurgents in areas declared as “disturbed” by the home ministry.
 
• AFSPA is invoked when a case of militancy or insurgency takes place and the territorial integrity of India is at risk.
 
• Security forces can “arrest a person without a warrant”, who has committed or is even “about to commit a cognizable offence” even based on “reasonable suspicion”.
 
• It also provides security forces with legal immunity for their actions in disturbed areas.
 
• In 1951, the Naga National Council (NNC) reported that it conducted a “free and fair plebiscite” in which about 99% of Nagas voted for a ‘Free Sovereign Naga Nation’.
 
• There was a boycott of the first general election of 1952 which later extended to a boycott of government schools and officials.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• AFSPA became law on September 11, 1958.
 
• Initially, it applied to the seven Northeastern states of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura. Hence, Option 1 is correct.
 
• This was so because in all these states there were movements of ethnic groups demanding separation from India.
 
• The government felt that such insurgencies could be checked through the deployment of the armed forces, and they would need special powers to carry out their responsibilities.
 
• AFSPA was extended to J&K in 1990, on similar considerations.
